anti_patterns: Skipping emitter registration checks: verifying Guardian signatures but accepting VAAs from any emitter lets anyone with a valid VAA from an unrelated app drive your contract
Sequence-based replay protection on non-finalized messages: sequence numbers are only unique after finality, so instant-consistency VAAs need hash-based replay protection
Treating relayer delivery as authenticity: the Executor/relayer is untrusted transport, validity comes only from Guardian signatures verified via the Core Contract
Ignoring consistency level on receipt: acting on a VAA attested under instant finality as if the source event cannot reorg
Hardcoding the Guardian set: rotation via governance breaks verification pinned to a stale set index, use getCurrentGuardianSetIndex
Storing large payloads on-chain: VAAs should carry references or compact instructions, bulk data belongs off-chain
avoid_when: Messages stay within a single chain or a single trust domain with shared consensus
Sub-second deterministic finality is required and attestation plus relay latency is unacceptable
No tolerance for threshold-trust assumptions and a fully trustless light-client proof is mandated
Throughput demands exceed per-message on-chain signature verification budgets
The deployment cannot operate Guardian full-node observation or permissionless relayer infrastructure
benefits: Chain agnosticism: one Core Contract interface spans EVM, Solana and other runtimes without pairwise bridges
Attestation/transport separation: Guardians sign while any permissionless relayer or the Executor marketplace delivers, so delivery competition cannot forge messages
Multicast by default: a single VAA verifies as authentic on every connected chain, avoiding n-squared pairwise integrations
Per-message finality control: the emitter's consistency level trades attestation latency against reorg risk per use case
Reusable token layer: Wrapped and Native Token Transfers build on the same VAA primitive instead of bespoke bridges
Defense in depth: the Governor rate-limits suspicious flows and the Global Accountant enforces supply invariants across chains
best_practices: Register trusted emitters per source chain and reject VAAs from unknown emitter address and chain pairs
Match replay protection to finality: sequence-based tracking for finalized VAAs, hash-based for instant consistency levels
Verify VAAs through the Core Contract's parseAndVerifyVM and check guardian set index, quorum and digest explicitly
Request conservative consistency levels for high-value transfers and accept slower attestation
Disable legacy automatic relaying when migrating to the Executor so exactly one delivery path handles each transfer
Track Guardian set rotations and delegated-chain threshold changes via governance announcements
Demand signed Executor quotes per request and treat expired quotes as failed deliveries
component_types: Emitter Contract: application contract that calls publishMessage on the source Core Contract
Core Contract: on-chain contract on every chain that publishes events and verifies VAAs via parseAndVerifyVM
Guardian Node: one of 19 validators running full nodes and signing observed messages over a P2P gossip network
Guardian Watcher: per-chain daemon enforcing the requested consistency level before signing

VAA (Verifiable Action Approval): header with guardian set index plus signatures wrapping a deterministic body of emitter chain, emitter address, sequence, timestamp, nonce, consistency level and payload
Relayer / Executor: permissionless off-chain transport fetching VAAs via Guardian RPC, Spy daemons or the Wormholescan API and submitting them to the target chain
Receiving Contract: target-chain logic that verifies the VAA, checks the registered emitter and replay state, then executes
Governor and Global Accountant: Guardian-side flow monitoring and cross-chain supply invariant enforcement delaying or blocking suspicious transfers
context: Independent blockchains with no shared consensus or trust need to exchange arbitrary messages and value. Contracts on one chain cannot read another chain's state, so a canonical off-chain validator set (the 19 Wormhole Guardians) observes source-chain events, attests with a 13-of-19 threshold signature forming a VAA, and target-chain contracts verify those signatures on-chain before acting.
design_principles: Threshold Attestation: no single observer can speak for a foreign chain, only a supermajority quorum of 13 of 19 Guardians produces a valid message
Separation of Attestation and Transport: signing proves authenticity while untrusted relayers provide availability, and neither can substitute for the other
Multicast Authenticity: a VAA attests that a contract on a chain said something, verifiable on any chain without addressing a destination
Deterministic Bodies: every Guardian derives the identical message body from the same finalized event so signatures aggregate over one digest
Explicit Finality Choice: each emission declares the source-finality commitment Guardians must wait for before signing
Receiver-Side Authorization: the target contract, not the network, decides which emitters are trusted and whether a VAA was already consumed

technology_stack: Guardian Network nodes with per-chain full nodes
Native Token Transfers (NTT) managers and transceivers
Spy daemons for Guardian gossip observation
tradeoffs: Threshold trust assumption: forging a VAA requires compromising 7 of 19 Guardians, so quorum collusion or key theft breaks every connected app at once
Validator set capped at 19: on-chain t-Schnorr multisig verification cost grows linearly per signer, limiting decentralization headroom
Finality latency tax: conservative consistency levels delay attestation until the source chain is deeply confirmed
Liveness depends on untrusted relayers: censored or crashed delivery stalls messages even though it cannot forge them
Receiver-side burden: every app must implement emitter registration and sequence- or hash-based replay protection itself
Verifier implementation risk: the February 2022 Solana sysvar-spoofing bug let an attacker mint 120,000 unbacked wETH (~$320M) without any Guardian signatures
Governance concentration: the same Guardian supermajority upgrades Core contracts and rotates the set via governance VAAs
Delegated observation weakens per-chain assumptions: delegated chains rely on a smaller observation subset before the canonical 13-of-19 sign
use_cases: Bridging tokens between chains via wrapped (WTT) or native (NTT) transfers attested by Guardian quorum
Cross-chain governance where a vote on one chain executes upgrades on many chains via governance VAAs
Multichain state reads letting a contract consume Guardian-attested data from a foreign chain
Pyth-style price or data feeds published once and verified as authentic on every connected chain
Cross-chain application messaging with Executor-based permissionless delivery and signed execution quotes
